scope: One bounded Tailscale-down fault was applied to an already running synthetic Kata job on the existing private Linux host. The root-only driver used the installed Jobs path, installed watchdog socket and service cgroup, and a private copy of the approved synthetic JSON fixture with a guest delay. It did not use OIDC, a browser, or a model call.

initial_idle_probe.limits: This had no active Kata job and did not test delegated execution termination.

active_probe.eventual_run_resolution: failed/null with explicitly unknown execution outcome after root-only inspection

diagnostic_findings: The watchdog's old generic error combines service termination verification and exact-resource cleanup failures. The retained journal reports SIGKILL and the generic error about 0.12 seconds apart, before the service unit completed its stop. This timing suggests a stop-verification race but does not identify the failing substep.

The original 30-second test checks disappearance of container metadata through nerdctl. It does not independently pin the Kata QEMU and shim process identities or establish the host execution termination deadline.
The later failed/null resolution and empty namespace show recovery after the failed observation, not timely cleanup. The execution outcome is unknown.
limits: Do not count this as a passing host-disconnect or 30-second termination check.
The active diagnostic supplied synthetic owner scope directly and did not exercise named-recipient browser authorization or a live model call.
The retained timestamps are observations for this run, not an SLA or proof of absolute safety.
One additional synthetic project/chat/run and audit events remain in the live database; no private project content was used.
privacy: This record contains no cloud project or instance name, account, credential, private URL, run ID, container ID, or transcript.

first_script_attempt.reason: The script expected 17 baseline runs while the live database had 18.

corrected_script_attempt.journal_observation: A containerd journal entry in the same second records a delete cleanup helper for the same container ID. This may explain the group reconstruction observation; exact monitoring evidence is insufficient to establish that explanation.
corrected_script_attempt.whole_group_acceptance_observation: Group reconstruction was observed when the pinned group exited at about 1.212 seconds, and the script immediately returned a failed 30-second whole-group acceptance; no direct whole-group observation was made at t=30 seconds.

resolution_and_recovery.resolver_automatic_cleanup: Ended with CalledProcessError; final service state was not automatically restored.
resolution_and_recovery.manual_resolution: Resolved the exact synthetic run to failed/null with execution outcome unknown.

follow_up: Add candidate identity logging so cleanup helpers and reconstructed groups can be attributed to the exact pinned job group.
Require and verify watchdog socket readiness before invoking the resolver.

candidate_observations.disposition: Unknown child is not trusted or accepted; classification is required.

third_active_attempt.acceptance_observation: The harness returned soon after original processes and candidate processes exited; it did not directly observe the whole group at t=30 seconds.
third_active_attempt.raw_evidence: Retained root-only with mode 0600 on the private host; raw evidence is not in the repository.
follow_up: Classify the unknown child under a fixed allowlist; keep unknown processes untrusted and fail-closed.
Add a direct observation through the full 30-second window.

documented_containerd_context.summary: The Runtime v2 documentation describes the shim delete subcommand as cleanup when containerd can no longer communicate with a shim, including after a shim is SIGKILLed.
documented_containerd_context.limit: This general documented behavior does not establish why the exact-ID helper was observed in this run and does not classify the separate unknown child.

observation.sampling_limit: The 0.175-second maximum scan gap bounds the observation cadence; it does not prove no transient execution occurred between scans.

untrusted_candidate.identity_observation: A private bounded identity check recorded executable/argv basename nerdctl with 7 arguments.
untrusted_candidate.disposition: Untrusted; do not accept as cleanup or infer that it re-executed the guest.

recovery_actions: Restarted tailscaled with Shields Up true and confirmed Running/Online.
Confirmed the Kata namespace empty and database integrity ok.
delayed_independent_postcheck_about_two_.tailnet_loss_root_cause: Unproven; do not attribute to PollNetMap EOF.

bounded_stability_observation.scope: Five-minute bounded observation only; longer-term stability and the earlier tailnet-loss root cause remain unresolved.

follow_up: Classify the untrusted nerdctl descendant under a fixed allowlist and do not accept unknown processes.
Investigate the later fixed-tailnet-state loss without asserting a root cause.

process_observation.sampling_limit: Zero reconstructed candidates were observed during bounded polling. A 0.183-second maximum scan gap does not prove that none could exist between scans.

limits: This bounded pass does not establish a universal hard 30-second SLA.
Bounded polling does not prove zero transient execution between scans.
The synthetic root-only path did not exercise browser/OIDC entry or a production user program.
This does not establish broader owner acceptance or pilot readiness.
The fourth attempt's delayed tailnet relapse remains preserved; its root cause is unknown.

read_only_journal_findings: At the fourth attempt's delayed failure, the watchdog logged that fixed private tailnet state was lost and stopped the Prism service.
In the same second, Tailscale logged a PollNetMap unexpected EOF. This ordering does not prove that the control-plane EOF caused the watchdog probe failure.

The lifecycle close path attempted to shield inbound traffic, could not complete its two normal close paths, and deliberately sent SIGKILL to tailscaled through its emergency-block branch. The tailscaled death was a fail-closed action, not evidence that the daemon spontaneously crashed.

The old watchdog journal did not distinguish a CLI timeout, command error, malformed response, backend/offline state, pinned identity mismatch or preference mismatch. The exact initiating condition therefore remains unknown.
delayed_relapse_diagnosis_follow_up.diagnostic_change: The watchdog now reports a fixed, secret-free probe category after stopping the service. The lifecycle close hook reports fixed categories when both normal shielding paths fail before emergency blocking. Neither change relaxes fail-closed checks or logs raw CLI output, addresses or credentials.

initial_diagnostic_release_superseded_af.service_and_watchdog_unit_diff: Only immutable release and record hashes/paths changed; project pin and 1000-cent model budget were preserved.
review_findings: A journal write failure could have prevented the emergency block in the close hook.
Stopped/offline Tailscale responses missing optional identity fields could have been misclassified as malformed responses.

reviewed_diagnostic_release.service_and_watchdog_unit_diff: Only immutable release and record hashes/paths changed; the project pin and 1000-cent model budget were preserved.

limits: The initiating condition of the delayed fourth-attempt shutdown remains undetermined; a later fixed category can distinguish future occurrences but cannot retroactively identify this one.
The installed diagnostic release has not been exercised by a new injected tailnet fault or authenticated browser/OIDC fault test.
This follow-up is observability and a normal-path deployment check, not proof of host-disconnect reliability, a hard SLA or pilot readiness.
